blind_target.authors: Maloney, L. T., & Dal Martello, M. F.
blind_target.title: Kin recognition and the perceived facial similarity of children
blind_target.evidence_quote: Facial similarity between individuals informs kinship judgments in third-party kin recognition. Indeed, one study found that similarity and kinship judgments encapsulate the same information (Maloney & Dal Martello, 2006). Yet, another study found that this is not the case when comparing adult face pairs of different sex (DeBruine et al., 2009). We replicated these studies to further clarify the role of facial similarity in kin recognition.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
In conclusion, using a larger stimuli sample of children, we replicated Maloney and Dal Martello's (
2006
) finding that kinship and similarity ratings are highly correlated. We found that the effect of sex was the same on similarity and on kinship judgments, contrary to
DeBruine et al (2009)
. However, we found that the effect of age was different on similarity judgments than on kinship judgments, contrary to
Maloney and Dal Martello (2006)
.

prior_decision.reason: The paper explicitly states that it replicates Maloney and Dal Martello's (2006) child-face study alongside DeBruine et al. (2009), and compares its correlation and age-difference results directly against Maloney and Dal Martello (2006), making it an omitted replication target with a mixed outcome.

luna_triage.reason: The abstract explicitly says the study replicated Maloney and Dal Martello (2006), and the Discussion reports both agreement with their highly correlated kinship/similarity ratings and a contrary age-effect result. The identity is established by the source's reference; the sole supplied shipped row is DeBruine et al. (2009), a different original. The prior adjudication correctly flagged the Maloney row as missing, and this recheck confirms it.
luna_triage.omission_quote: In conclusion, using a larger stimuli sample of children, we replicated Maloney and Dal Martello's (2006) finding that kinship and similarity ratings are highly correlated. We found that the effect of sex was the same on similarity and on kinship judgments, contrary to DeBruine et al (2009). However, we found that the effect of age was different on similarity judgments than on kinship judgments, contrary to Maloney and Dal Martello (2006).
luna_triage.identity_quote: Maloney and Dal Martello (2006) found that pairs receiving higher similarity ratings were also judged to be siblings more often, whereas pairs receiving lower similarity ratings were judged to be siblings less often.
